description: Build a Python CLI and schema-driven benchmark harness for packaging sanitized historical Web3 vulnerable source snapshots, running AI security tools against them without leakage, and scoring submitted findings against private oracle records. Use Python 3.12 with Typer for the CLI, Pydantic/jsonschema for validation, pytest for tests, and Docker/network isolation where needed.

userStories.title: Create Python CLI project skeleton
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a maintainable Python CLI foundation so future stories can add benchmark packaging and evaluation commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a Python 3.12 project configuration with package metadata and console entrypoint named sol-audit-challenges
Use Typer or an equivalent lightweight CLI framework
Add pytest-based test scaffolding
Add README instructions for installing and running the CLI locally
Run the available tests or validation checks successfully

userStories.title: Validate public and private manifests
userStories.description: As a curator, I need CLI validation for public challenge manifests and private oracle files so malformed benchmark data is caught before packaging or scoring.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a CLI command that validates a public challenge manifest against schemas/public-challenge.schema.json
Add a CLI command that validates a private oracle file against schemas/private-oracle.schema.json
Validation errors include the file path and the failing schema location
Tests cover valid and invalid manifests
Run the available tests successfully

userStories.title: Prepare source snapshot from a vulnerable commit
userStories.description: As a curator, I need a command that exports a repository at a specific commit into a clean source snapshot without Git history.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a prepare-case command that accepts repo URL or local path, commit, case id, and output directory
The generated source snapshot contains files from the requested commit
The generated source snapshot does not contain .git, remotes, branches, tags, or commit history
The command writes a draft private oracle file outside the public bundle path
Tests cover local fixture repository export and confirm .git metadata is absent

userStories.title: Sanitize source snapshots for leakage
userStories.description: As a curator, I need repeatable sanitization rules that remove obvious incident clues while preserving buildable source code.
acceptanceCriteria: Add sanitizer configuration for removing or replacing files such as README, audits, docs, deployments, broadcast, cache, out, and known exploit artifacts
Add configurable string replacement rules for protocol names, incident names, addresses, and transaction hashes
Sanitizer produces a report of removed files and replacements without exposing private oracle data in public output
Tests cover removal rules and replacement rules
Run the available tests successfully

userStories.title: Build immutable challenge bundles
userStories.description: As a benchmark maintainer, I need sanitized snapshots packaged as deterministic archives with public manifests and checksums.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a bundle-case command that creates a tar.gz archive from a sanitized source snapshot
Archive contents are deterministic across repeated runs when inputs are unchanged
The command writes or updates a public challenge manifest with archive path and sha256
The archive excludes private oracle files, local research notes, .git metadata, and generated reports
Tests confirm checksum stability and excluded paths

userStories.title: Run tools in an isolated benchmark environment
userStories.description: As an evaluator, I need to run an AI security tool against a challenge bundle with no internet and no access to private oracle data.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a run-case command that extracts a challenge bundle into a temporary workspace
The runner supports a configurable command for the tool under test
The runner has a network-disabled Docker mode or clearly documented local no-network fallback
Only the public source snapshot and public manifest are mounted into the tool workspace
Run metadata and tool output are stored under reports or runs without modifying the source snapshot

userStories.title: Define finding submission format
userStories.description: As an evaluator, I need a structured report format for submitted findings so scoring can be consistent across tools.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a JSON schema for submitted findings
Submitted findings include title, affected files, root cause, impact, proof sketch, and optional reproduction steps
Add CLI validation for submitted finding reports
Add at least one example accepted-style finding report with fake data only
Tests cover valid and invalid finding reports

userStories.title: Score submitted findings against private oracle records
userStories.description: As a benchmark maintainer, I need an evaluator that compares submitted findings to private oracle records without exposing the oracle to the evaluated tool.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a score-report command that accepts a submitted finding report and a private oracle file
The scorer outputs accepted, partial, duplicate, false_positive, or out_of_scope statuses
Initial scoring may use deterministic keyword, location, and human-review fields rather than LLM judging
The scorer output includes enough explanation for maintainers without printing sensitive oracle fields by default
Tests cover accepted, partial, and false-positive examples using fake oracle data

userStories.title: Add private candidate research workflow
userStories.description: As a curator, I need a safe workflow for tracking candidate incidents, audit findings, source references, vulnerable commits, and verification status without committing answers publicly.
acceptanceCriteria: Document the private candidate research workflow and required verification steps
Add templates for ignored private candidate and oracle files
Ensure .gitignore prevents private candidate files, oracle files, and local research notes from being committed
Add a public fake candidate example that contains no real incident names or vulnerable commits
Run validation checks successfully

userStories.title: Add benchmark leakage audit command
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need an automated leakage check that warns when challenge bundles contain names, URLs, Git metadata, exploit artifacts, or other answer clues.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an audit-leakage command for source snapshots and archives
The command detects .git metadata, repository URLs, commit hashes, audit report filenames, incident keywords, addresses, and transaction hashes
The command supports a private denylist file that is never committed
The command produces a machine-readable report and a human-readable summary
Tests cover common leakage patterns

userStories.title: Add end-to-end fake benchmark fixture
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a complete fake vulnerable project fixture so the entire prepare, sanitize, bundle, run, submit, and score flow can be tested without real incident data.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a tiny fake Solidity or Python project fixture with an intentionally simple vulnerability
Add fake public manifest, private oracle, and submitted report examples
Add an end-to-end test that exercises the core CLI flow without network access
The fixture contains no real protocol names, incident names, addresses, or vulnerable commits
Run the full test suite successfully

userStories.title: Document operating model and security boundaries
userStories.description: As a benchmark operator, I need clear documentation for safely creating, distributing, and evaluating challenge cases without leaking ground truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Document the public repo, private curator repo, and generated artifact separation
Document how to run tools with network disabled and oracle files withheld
Document which case classes are high quality, low quality, or special handling such as compiler bugs
Document curator review checklist before publishing any challenge bundle
Docs link to the relevant CLI commands and schemas
